answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable reputation bond before it may submit bids, then slash that bond when a randomly audited task proves fraudulent. One person can still mint many identities, but each must immobilize real capital and each can lose it, so splitting into sybils no longer makes attacks cheap. The bond need not be saffron on an island in an ocean; its value comes from the credible, enforceable loss.
